current.text: There is talk that Bey could start for the Pelicans and close games in lineups with Zion Williamson at center.

Josh thinks there is far too much hype around Bey. He went for 1 USD in an expert auction mock draft. An earlier mock called him a bad pick at 119 because he might be only the seventh or eighth man on the Pelicans.

New Orleans has a crowded rotation of about eight players who could all start, including Bey. Bennedict Mathurin has also been added. There are too many players for 240 minutes, so roles are hard to project.
The latest expert lineup projection has Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy, Dejounte Murray and probably Yves Missi starting. The last spot goes to Jeremiah Fears or Herb Jones, not Bey.
The Pelicans have a new head coach, Jamahl Mosley, who brings a defense-first identity.
Experts see the Pelicans as a weak team near the bottom of the West. One projection is about 34 wins, which would not make the playoffs.

durable.text: He blocks almost no shots, even for a forward, so a punt BLK build loses little with him.

note: Bey sits right at our 144-player cut (Yahoo rank 151, ESPN rank 133), with 0 USD values and average costs of 1.0 USD on Yahoo and 0.2 USD on ESPN, so at most he is a 1 USD last pick. His projected line gives solid FT% and threes with few turnovers, but almost no blocks and a below-average FG%, so he fits punt BLK builds best. Experts doubt the starter hype, so leave him on waivers and watch early in the season whether Mosley starts him or closes games with him.
